name: Hall in Tirol Altstadt
kurzbeschreibung: The historic old town of Hall in Tyrol enchants as Western Austria's largest medieval ensemble, featuring Hasegg Castle, Mint Tower, and salt-trading alleys.
preis: Old town free of charge; Mint Museum & Tower adults €13.00, children €9.00
oeffnungszeiten: Old town open 24/7; Mint Museum at Hasegg Castle Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00 (winter Tue–Sat 10:00–17:00)
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic old town of Hall in Tirol—located in the scenic Inn Valley ten kilometers east of Innsbruck—represents the largest and best-preserved medieval architectural ensemble in Western Austria. Shaped by over seven centuries of heritage as a prosperous center of salt extraction, Inn river navigation, and imperial coinage, the pedestrianized city center resembles an authentic open-air museum of late-Gothic urban design. Harmoniously winding alleys, stately merchant townhouses with bay windows, stepped gables, and historic squares bestow Hall with an incomparable medieval flair. Adorned with picturesque fountains, secluded arched courtyards, and ornate wrought-iron guild signs, Hall is a haven for photographers and culture aficionados.

Route & Requirements

Hall's economic ascendancy was founded on salt: mining began in the Halltal valley in the 13th century, and city rights were granted in 1303. By the late Middle Ages, Hall stood as the central logistics port on the River Inn. In 1477, Archduke Sigmund transferred the sovereign mint to Hall, where in 1486 he struck the Guldiner—the world's first large silver coin, the direct ancestor of the Thaler and namesake of the US Dollar. From 1567 onward, Hasegg Castle served as the imperial mint where revolutionary roller-press coining was invented. The landmark of the city is the twelve-sided, 46-meter-high Mint Tower (Münzerturm). Other civic highlights include the Upper Town Square with the Gothic Town Hall (1447), St. Nicholas parish church, and Stiftsplatz. Hall was honored with the prestigious Austrian National Heritage Award.

Visit & Arrival

The pedestrian old town is freely accessible 24/7 year-round. The Hall Mint Museum and the Mint Tower at Hasegg Castle are open April to October Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (winter Tuesday to Saturday 10:00 to 17:00). Admission: adults €13.00, children €9.00; free with the Innsbruck Card. Guided heritage walks depart from the tourist office on Unterer Stadtplatz. Transit: S-Bahn from Innsbruck Central Station to Hall in Tirol (9 minutes), then 7 minutes walk to the center; buses 504 and 505 stop directly at Unterer Stadtplatz. By car: A12 autobahn (exit Hall Mitte), Altstadt underground garage.

Tips

The historic cobblestone paving is smooth and manageable with strollers; the Mint Museum on the ground floor is wheelchair accessible (the tower climb has 204 historic stairs). Soak up the ambiance in sidewalk cafés on the Upper Town Square, browse the Saturday farmers' market, or stop into a cozy traditional Tyrolean pastry bakery. In December, experience the romantic Hall Advent market when townhouse facades glow with festive lights.
